title: Cloud auto-scaling methods and research challenges
full_query:
I need you to help me research 'Auto-Scaling' technology in cloud computing. Please organize a clear report around this topic, mainly consisting of two major parts:

Part One: Categorize current mainstream auto-scaling technologies. To my knowledge, they are mainly divided into two broad categories: 'Reactive' and 'Proactive'. Under these two categories, please provide a detailed introduction to specific technical methods. For each technical method (e.g., threshold-based, machine learning-based, etc.), please explain its core working principle, main advantages, and limitations.

Part Two: Summarize the main challenges faced by academia and industry when applying auto-scaling, and the solutions proposed to address these challenges. Please cover at least the following challenge areas: energy efficiency, dynamic nature of telecom services, big data processing, cost-effective graph processing, and workload prediction. For each challenge, first describe the specific manifestation of the problem, and then find a specific, published research study as an example to illustrate the solution proposed by that research.

The final output should be divided into two main headings: 'Auto-Scaling Technology Classification' and 'Main Challenges and Solutions'. Under the first heading, further organize the content into two subheadings: 'Reactive Methods' and 'Proactive Methods'. Under the second heading, use each challenge as a subheading. The overall content should be clear, accurate, and robust with information.

**important**The following is a rule of highest priority that you must not violate. Please put this rule in your task plan and keep it in your memory: **During the research process, you are not allowed to view the following article and urls: {'title': 'Auto-Scaling Techniques in Cloud Computing: Issues and Research Directions', 'authors': ['Saleha Alharthi', 'Afra Alshamsi', 'Anoud Alseiari', 'Abdulmalik Alwarafy'], 'urls': ['https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/24/17/5551', 'https://www.researchgate.net/publication/383489546_Auto-Scaling_Techniques_in_Cloud_Computing_Issues_and_Research_Directions', 'https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39275461/', 'https://research.uaeu.ac.ae/en/publications/auto-scaling-techniques-in-cloud-computing-issues-and-research-di']}. Even if you accidentally read it, please ignore the content of the article and do not quote it.**

pointwise.title: Reactive and proactive classification
pointwise.question: Does the report distinguish reactive from proactive auto-scaling using the timing and information behind the scaling decision?

anchors.1: No usable classification.
anchors.2: Only the two category names appear.
anchors.3: A distinction is attempted but current-state response and anticipating demand remain confused.
anchors.4: Both categories and the basis of classification are clear, with a minor boundary ambiguity.
anchors.5: Explains response to observed conditions versus preparing for anticipated demand, and classifies the described implementations on that basis; hybrid behavior is identified when used.

pointwise.boundary: An algorithm name does not by itself determine the category. Do not require RL or fuzzy control to be inherently proactive.

provenance.change_note: Retains the requested categories and adds implementation-sensitive boundaries; anchors locally authored.

pointwise.title: Threshold-rule scaling
pointwise.question: Does the report explain threshold-rule scaling, its practical advantages and limitations?

anchors.1: No threshold-rule account.
anchors.2: Names thresholds without a trigger-to-action explanation.
anchors.3: Explains some of the rule-based method, but the trigger-to-action principle, deployment advantage or tuning/response limitation is substantively missing.
anchors.4: Explains metrics, rules, scaling action, simplicity and relevant limitations with a minor condition missing.
anchors.5: Explains the metric-rule-action loop and ease of deployment, with rule tuning, oscillation or provisioning-delay limits under changing demand.

pointwise.boundary: No fixed CPU value or vendor. Threshold control does not inevitably fail at every spike.

provenance.change_note: v3.3 targeted revision: Restore a specific family: principle without limitations is 3; another family cannot compensate for absence. Cross-review makes missing principle, benefit or limitation symmetric at 3.

pointwise.title: Predictive machine learning
pointwise.question: Does the report explain data-driven demand prediction and its scaling use, benefits and limits?

anchors.1: No predictive ML method.
anchors.2: Only names ML or an architecture.
anchors.3: Explains some predictive ML, but its learning-to-scaling principle, useful advance-capacity benefit or data/error limitation is substantively missing.
anchors.4: Connects features, prediction and advance action with benefits and limits; minor detail missing.
anchors.5: Explains learned demand prediction, its advance-capacity use and useful patterns, and how data quality, drift or forecast error can cause over/under-provisioning.

pointwise.boundary: No mandatory network/SVM/regression list. Distinguish learned prediction from action-policy learning; a combined method can explain both functions.

provenance.change_note: v3.3 targeted revision: Restore a specific family: principle without limitations is 3; another family cannot compensate for absence. Cross-review makes missing principle, benefit or limitation symmetric at 3.

pointwise.title: Energy efficiency challenge and study
pointwise.question: Does the report describe an auto-scaling energy-efficiency problem and explain a specific published study's proposed response?

anchors.2: Only says energy matters or names a paper.
anchors.3: Problem or study solution is concrete, but the other is missing or their connection is unclear.
anchors.4: Energy problem, identifiable study and proposed scaling response are connected, with minor setting detail missing.
anchors.5: Explains where resources waste energy or scaling creates an energy trade-off, identifies a published study and describes how its proposal addresses that problem in its stated setting.

pointwise.boundary: No mandatory Hadoop/storage-compute separation route. Publication identity must be sufficient to find the study; its support is checked separately.

provenance.change_note: Retains energy problem and a study-backed response; relaxes the specified Hadoop paper and architecture. Cross-review maps the challenge-coverage portion of presentation:5 here; heading form stays in PT.D1.09.

pointwise.title: Telecom dynamics challenge and study
pointwise.question: Does the report describe how changing telecom service demands challenge scaling and illustrate a solution from a specific published study?

anchors.2: Only says telecom traffic is dynamic.
anchors.3: A concrete telecom issue or study is given, but not a clear problem-to-solution connection.
anchors.4: Telecom service dynamics, study and proposed scaling behavior are clear, with minor operational context missing.
anchors.5: Describes the relevant changing service workload or provisioning requirements, identifies a published telecom study and explains its response in the stated service environment.

pointwise.boundary: Do not require 5G, VNFs and CNFs all together, a unified resource pool, or a particular load balancer.

provenance.change_note: Retains telecom-specific problem and published example while removing the prescribed architecture. Cross-review maps the challenge-coverage portion of presentation:5 here; heading form stays in PT.D1.09.

pointwise.title: Big-data processing challenge and study

anchors.4: Big-data workload issue and study response are connected, with minor execution-context gaps.
anchors.5: Explains the processing workload and resource mismatch, identifies a published study, and describes its scaling response and operating setting.

pointwise.boundary: Batch and stream routes remain eligible. Do not require Hadoop, CEAS or a claim that every fixed allocation wastes resources.

provenance.change_note: Uses the resource/workload mismatch and research-response objects; does not require CEAS. Cross-review maps the challenge-coverage portion of presentation:5 here; heading form stays in PT.D1.09.

pointwise.title: Cost-effective graph processing challenge and study

anchors.4: Graph workload, cost issue and study response are clear, with a minor condition missing.
anchors.5: Explains a graph-specific scaling cost tension, identifies a published study and describes the proposed resource or execution response in its setting.

pointwise.boundary: Do not force heterogeneous VMs, repartitioning or a specific author. Generic big-data cost text does not substitute for the graph problem.

pointwise.title: Workload prediction challenge and study

pointwise.boundary: No mandatory SVM classifier or accuracy number; prediction methods and deployment contexts may differ.

provenance.change_note: Retains forecasting challenge, provision consequences and study response; removes SVM as compulsory solution. Cross-review maps the challenge-coverage portion of presentation:5 here; heading form stays in PT.D1.09.
